    Rescaling the meshes of ℤΔ to the signed coefficients #

    Proof of Proposition 4.1, Step 2 (periodic-mesh-calculations.tex): "We first rescale the meshes on ℤΔ to the coefficients ±1 ... On a tree edge u → v, write the repetition arrows as a_j : u_j → v_j and b_j : v_j → u_{j+1}. The two coefficients at its endpoints prescribe nonzero products ... Their ratio determines μ_{a,j} recursively in both directions from μ_{a,0}, and then determines every μ_b. There is no periodic equation on the integer line, and different tree edges have disjoint arrow variables."

    In height coordinates the arrows over an edge {x, y} form a line indexed by the height h of their source, and the mesh at height h + 2 prescribes the product of the scalars of the arrows of heights h and h + 1 (exists_line_solution).

    source
    theorem MultiplicativeBasisDeformations.exists_line_solution {k : Type u} [CommRing k] (r : ℤ → kˣ) :
    ∃ (m : ℤ → kˣ), ∀ (s : ℤ), m s * m (s + 1) = r s

    No periodic equation on the integer line: any prescribed products of consecutive terms are realized.
